verses.1: G I have come to my garden, my sister, my bride; I gather my myrrh and my spices, I eat my honey and my sweetmeats, I drink my wine and my milk. D Eat, friends; drink! Drink freely of love!
verses.2: B I was sleeping, but my heart kept vigil; I heard my lover knocking: "Open to me, my sister, my beloved, my dove, my perfect one! For my head is wet with dew, my locks with the moisture of the night."
verses.3: I have taken off my robe, am I then to put it on? I have bathed my feet, am I then to soil them?
verses.4: My lover put his hand through the opening; my heart trembled within me, and I grew faint when he spoke.
verses.5: I rose to open to my lover, with my hands dripping myrrh: With my fingers dripping choice myrrh upon the fittings of the lock.
verses.6: I opened to my lover - but my lover had departed, gone. I sought him but I did not find him; I called to him but he did not answer me.
verses.7: The watchmen came upon me as they made their rounds of the city; They struck me, and wounded me, and took my mantle from me, the guardians of the walls.
verses.8: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, if you find my lover - What shall you tell him?- that I am faint with love.
verses.9: D How does your lover differ from any other, O most beautiful among women? How does your lover differ from any other, that you adjure us so?
verses.10: B My lover is radiant and ruddy; he stands out among thousands.
verses.11: His head is pure gold; his locks are palm fronds, black as the raven.
verses.12: His eyes are like doves beside running waters, His teeth would seem bathed in milk, and are set like jewels.
verses.13: His cheeks are like beds of spice with ripening aromatic herbs. His lips are red blossoms; they drip choice myrrh.
verses.14: His arms are rods of gold adorned with chrysolites. His body is a work of ivory covered with sapphires.
verses.15: His legs are columns of marble resting on golden bases. His stature is like the trees on Lebanon, imposing as the cedars.
verses.16: His mouth is sweetness itself; he is all delight. Such is my lover, and such my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.

notes.text: Eat, friends; drink!: the lovers are encouraged to enjoy the delights of their love, symbol of Christ's union with the Church.
A trial similar to that in Song 3:1-5.
The bride's hesitation is due, not to levity, but to strong emotion.
The disappearance of the lover seems to be a deliberate trial and test inflicted on the girl.
The watchmen do not know the reason for the girl's appearance in the city streets; cf Song 3:2-4.
In answer to the question of Song 5:9 the girl sings her lover's praises (Song 5:10-16). Gold: indicates how precious the lover is. Palm fronds: his thick, luxuriant growth of hair.
